title: Dotnet Programming · Chapter 1
description: .NET technology (CLR, FCL, CLS, languages, C#), static vs dynamic web pages, ASP.NET, advantages and PHP vs .NET.

topics.title: 1.1 What Is .NET?
topics.description: .NET as a platform, its languages and platforms, origin, what you can build, the .NET Framework and its design features.

questions.prompt: What is .NET?

options.text: A unified, open-source developer platform by Microsoft for building, deploying and running applications in several languages
A single programming language for web pages
A database system made by Microsoft

questions.explanation: .NET is a developer platform supporting several languages (C#, VB.NET, F#).

questions.prompt: Which LANGUAGES does .NET support, according to your notes? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: C#, VB.NET and F#. (.NET Core, .NET Framework and Xamarin are PLATFORMS, not languages.)

questions.prompt: Which are .NET PLATFORMS listed in your notes? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: C# is a language and Visual Studio is an IDE.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, when did Microsoft announce .NET?
questions.explanation: Announced by Microsoft in July 2000.

questions.prompt: What was .NET originally designed to do?

options.text: Bridge the gap in interoperability between services written in different languages

questions.explanation: Its goal was interoperability across languages.

questions.prompt: What can you build with .NET (WMDMGMCI)? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Web, Mobile, Desktop, Microservices, Game development, Machine learning, Cloud, Internet of Things.

questions.prompt: In “What can I build with .NET”, what does IoT stand for?
questions.explanation: IoT = Internet of Things.

questions.prompt: What is the .NET Framework?

options.text: A software development platform for building and running Windows applications, with languages, libraries and developer tools

questions.explanation: It includes the CLR, which manages execution of all apps built with the .NET library.

questions.prompt: Which part of the .NET Framework maintains the execution of all applications developed using the .NET library?
questions.explanation: The CLR runs .NET applications.

questions.prompt: What are the design features of the .NET Framework (IPSMST)? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: IPSMST. Memory is managed automatically (garbage collection), not freed by hand.

questions.prompt: What are the two MAIN components of the .NET Framework? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: CLR + FCL.

topics.title: 1.1 CLR & FCL
topics.description: What the CLR does, JIT compilation, its eight components, and the Framework Class Library.

questions.prompt: What does CLR stand for?
questions.explanation: CLR = Common Language Runtime.

questions.prompt: The CLR is a common runtime environment for all .NET languages, built on…
questions.explanation: CTS defines the types all .NET languages share.

questions.prompt: What does the Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler do?

options.text: Converts managed Intermediate Language (IL / MSIL) code into native machine code at runtime

questions.explanation: .NET code compiles to IL first; the JIT turns IL into native code when it runs.

questions.prompt: .NET source code is first compiled into which form, before the JIT runs it?
questions.explanation: Source → IL (managed code) → JIT → native code.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, the CLR supports how many languages? (number)
questions.explanation: 36+ languages.

questions.prompt: How does the CLR prevent memory leaks?

options.text: The programmer frees every object by hand

questions.explanation: Memory allocation and garbage collection are automated.

questions.prompt: The CLR allows cross-language inheritance and debugging between .NET languages.
questions.explanation: Interoperability is a core CLR feature.

questions.prompt: Which are components of the CLR (EOIMSEIM)? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: The eight CLR components are Execution engine, OS interface, IL translation, Memory allocation, Security, Exception handling, Interoperability and Metadata support.

questions.prompt: Which CLR component connects .NET applications directly with the operating system?
Which CLR component translates IL code into native machine language for the target hardware?
Which CLR component lets .NET work with COM components and DLLs?
questions.explanation: COM = Component Object Model; DLL = Dynamic Link Library.

questions.prompt: Which CLR component provides information needed for runtime inspection, reflection and type safety?
Which CLR component enforces code identity, access permissions and type-safety boundaries?
What does FCL stand for?
questions.explanation: FCL = Framework Class Library.

questions.prompt: What is the FCL?

options.text: A huge collection of reusable classes, interfaces, namespaces and value types

questions.explanation: A consistent, object-oriented library of prepackaged functionality.

questions.prompt: How are FCL classes accessed?
questions.explanation: e.g. `using System;` gives access to the System namespace.

questions.prompt: What kinds of applications can you develop with the class library? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: From your notes.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, the class library contains more than how many classes?
questions.explanation: More than 7000 classes.

questions.prompt: The classes let a .NET app do which of these? (select all that apply)

options.text: Read and write types of data

questions.explanation: From your notes' list.

topics.title: 1.1 Architecture, CLS, Languages & C#
topics.description: The .NET Framework stack, the Common Language Specification, Visual Studio .NET languages and C# features.

questions.prompt: In the .NET Framework architecture stack, what is the BOTTOM (foundation) layer?
questions.explanation: Bottom: Base Class Library → middle: ADO.NET and XML → top: ASP.NET and Windows Forms.

questions.prompt: Which layer sits in the MIDDLE of the stack (data access)?
Which sit in the TOP layer (application models)? (select all that apply)

options.text: ASP.NET (Web Forms, Web Services, Mobile Internet Toolkit)

questions.explanation: ASP.NET and Windows Forms sit side by side above ADO.NET and XML.

questions.prompt: What does CLS stand for?
questions.explanation: CLS = Common Language Specification.

questions.prompt: What is the CLS?

options.text: A set of basic language features/rules that .NET languages must follow, converting their syntax rules into a CLR-understandable format

questions.explanation: It lets objects written in different languages interact.

questions.prompt: What are the functions of the CLS? (select all that apply)

options.text: An object-oriented model supporting many languages

questions.explanation: Garbage collection is a CLR job.

questions.prompt: Which are the BASIC .NET languages listed under CLS? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Perl and Smalltalk are among the 36+ OTHER languages.

questions.prompt: What is Visual Studio .NET?

options.text: An Integrated Development Environment (IDE) to build, compile and run .NET apps

questions.prompt: What does IDE stand for?

Which Visual Studio .NET language gives system-level access and high performance?

C# syntax is very similar to…
questions.explanation: C# is a modern, managed, object-oriented language by Microsoft.

questions.prompt: What is C#'s language philosophy? (select all that apply)
Which are the features of C# (SMOTVCS)? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: SMOTVCS.

topics.title: 1.2 Web-Based Applications: Static vs Dynamic
topics.description: The UTHM / SMAP scenario, static and dynamic web pages, how each is served, and server-side technology.

questions.prompt: What is a web application?

options.text: An application accessed through a web browser

questions.prompt: Ali reads general information about UTHM before registering. Every visitor sees the same content. What kind of page is it?
questions.explanation: It shows fixed information and doesn't need individual user information.

questions.prompt: After logging in, SMAP UTHM shows Ali his own profile and registered courses. Why can it do this?

options.text: It uses user accounts and server-side processing to generate personalised pages
It stores a separate HTML file for every student on Ali's computer

questions.explanation: Dynamic pages are built on the server per request.

questions.prompt: What is the MAIN difference between how static and dynamic pages are served?

options.text: Static pages are faster to type
Static: the server returns a stored HTML file unchanged. Dynamic: the server runs server-side code first to generate the HTML

questions.explanation: Dynamic pages add a server-side processing step before the HTML is sent.

questions.prompt: Static web pages are written with which languages? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: PHP and ASP.NET are dynamic (server-side).

questions.prompt: A static web page uses a database to build its content at runtime.
questions.explanation: Static pages return predefined content with no database queries or application logic.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order for serving a STATIC page?

options.text: Author writes HTML → client requests page → server locates the file → server returns the unmodified HTML → browser renders it
Client requests → server runs code → database query → HTML generated → browser renders
Server locates file → author writes HTML → browser renders → client requests
Browser renders → server returns HTML → client requests

questions.prompt: Which technologies are used for DYNAMIC web pages in your notes? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Also ASP and AJAX.

questions.prompt: Which are examples of dynamic websites? (select all that apply)

options.text: A one-page poster that never changes

questions.explanation: Also community portals.

questions.prompt: What are the key capabilities of dynamic web pages? (select all that apply)
What does server-side technology enable?

options.text: The browser can work without a server
The web server can generate HTML on the fly

questions.explanation: It adds an extra layer to static pages.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order of how server-side technology works?

options.text: Send response → generate HTML → interpret code
Generate HTML → interpret code → send response
Send response → interpret code → generate HTML
Interpret server-side code → generate appropriate HTML → send the response to the browser

questions.prompt: When serving a DYNAMIC page, what does the server do after locating the page?

options.text: Collects the contents (code + HTML), parses and processes them to produce HTML
Asks the user to write the HTML

questions.prompt: In both static and dynamic serving, the browser finally receives HTML and renders it.
questions.explanation: Server-side code never reaches the browser; only the resulting HTML does.

questions.prompt: Which diagram shows a DYNAMIC web page being served?

image.alt: A laptop sends a REQUEST to a web server; the server sends a request to an application script (gear) that exchanges data with a database, then the server sends a RESPONSE back.
A laptop sends a REQUEST to a web server with a file folder, and the server sends a RESPONSE straight back.

questions.explanation: The dynamic version passes the request to an application script that talks to a database before the server responds.

questions.prompt: In the dynamic diagram, which component processes the request and interacts with the database?

image.alt: Static: the laptop sends a request to the web server, which sends back pre-written HTML files directly. Dynamic: the laptop requests from the web server, which passes a request to an application script; the script works with a database and returns a response, and the server sends back a custom HTML page.
image.caption: Static vs dynamic page serving

questions.explanation: Server-side scripts generate a custom HTML page from script and database data.

questions.prompt: In the static diagram, what does the web server send back?

image.alt: Static: the laptop sends a request to the web server, which sends back pre-written HTML files directly. Dynamic: the laptop requests from the web server, which passes a request to an application script; the script works with a database and returns a response, and the server sends back a custom HTML page.
image.caption: Static vs dynamic page serving

options.text: A page generated from a database

questions.prompt: Which components appear ONLY in the dynamic serving process? (select all that apply)

image.alt: Static: the laptop sends a request to the web server, which sends back pre-written HTML files directly. Dynamic: the laptop requests from the web server, which passes a request to an application script; the script works with a database and returns a response, and the server sends back a custom HTML page.

topics.title: 1.3 Introduction to ASP.NET
topics.description: What ASP.NET is, its foundations, capabilities, .aspx pages and how an ASP.NET request is processed.

questions.prompt: What is ASP.NET?

options.text: A Microsoft .NET technology for creating interactive and dynamic web pages

questions.prompt: ASP.NET is a convergence of which two Microsoft technologies? (select all that apply)
What does ASP stand for?
questions.explanation: ASP = Active Server Pages.

questions.prompt: ASP.NET is built on top of…
Which languages can you program ASP.NET in? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Any .NET language.

questions.prompt: What capabilities does ASP.NET have? (select all that apply)

options.text: A large set of rich web controls

questions.prompt: ASP.NET web pages are saved with which file extension?
Why is ASP.NET fast?

options.text: It runs entirely in the browser

questions.explanation: Compiled execution increases performance.

questions.prompt: What is the correct order when an ASP.NET page is requested?

options.text: Web server sends HTML → browser requests → engine executes → file retrieved
Browser requests → web server retrieves the file → forwards it to the ASP.NET script engine → engine executes it → HTML is generated and returned to the server → server sends HTML to the client
Engine executes → browser requests → server retrieves → HTML sent
Browser requests → server sends the .aspx code to the browser → browser executes it

questions.explanation: The browser only ever receives HTML.

questions.prompt: Which part reads the ASP.NET file from top to bottom and executes it?
The web browser receives and runs the .aspx code directly.
questions.explanation: The server-side engine runs it; the browser receives only the resulting HTML.

questions.prompt: What does IIS stand for?

questions.prompt: Which describes PHP, according to your notes?

options.text: A framework supporting multiple languages only on Windows
An HTML-embedded scripting language that runs on any OS and HTTP server, free of cost
A proprietary framework that needs software licences
